newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: Guatemala faces post-war challenges says President.
newsitem.headline: Guatemala faces post-war challenges says President.

text.p: Guatemala will only be beginning to solve its economic and social problems after the government and leftist rebels sign a peace agreement in December, President Alvaro Arzu said on Tuesday.
"Manna from heaven will not fall the day after the peace accord," Arzu told reporters at a news conference on his return from an Ibero-American summit in Chile, where he met with regional leaders.
"But it was impossible to begin to solve Guatemala's underlying problems without signing the accord," he said.

Arzu announced on Monday in Chile that peace negotiating teams of the government and the Guatemalan National Revolutionary Unit (URNG) had agreed to sign a definitve peace accord in Guatemala on Dec. 29.
Complex peace negotations, including 11 separate accords on everything from Indian rights to army troop reductions, have dragged on since 1991.
Arzu said on Tuesday that Guatemalans should not have false expectations for the post-war era.
The government is seeking international aid, as well as increasing its own social services budget, in order to fulfil ambitious promises in the accords.

In the peace agreements, the government has promised to take on expensive projects such as aid for tens of thousands of people displaced in the war, and raising the literacy rate from under 50 percent to more than 70 percent.

Central America's only remaining civil war began 36 years ago with an estimated death and disappeared toll of 140,000. The violence peaked in the early 1980s when the army massacred thousands of poor, Indian villagers in an attempt to eliminate guerrilla sympathisers.
